items.title: Retail industry welcomes shoplifting decrease with caution
items.summary: The latest ONS crime stats show that, following a period of increases in shoplifting, there has been a 2% decrease (to 519,516 offences) in the year ending June 2026, when compared with the previous year (530,336 offences). Recent increases in police recorded shoplifting likely reflect… This story continues at Retail industry welcomes shoplifting decrease with caution Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
Recent increases in police recorded shoplifting likely reflect both growth in offences and improved reporting resulting from closer engagement between police and retailers.
Reporting rates for shoplifting are known to be very low and police are actively encouraging the reporting of all incidents and the submission of supporting evidence, such as CCTV, to strengthen intelligence, identify offenders, and link related offences.
The Crime Survey for England and Wales also show a 10% increase in the overall number of robbery offences recorded.
Responding to the figures, Lucy Whing, crime policy adviser at the British Retail Consortium (BRC), said: “Retailers will welcome today’s figures, but progress on tackling shop theft is still too slow.
“Theft is not a victimless crime: it fuels violence against shop workers, and adds costs that ultimately hit shoppers’ pockets. With 1,600 incidents of violence or abuse against retail workers every day, the human toll remains unacceptable.
“The Crime and Policing Act granted police new powers to intervene and prosecute offenders, including a long-overdue offence of assaulting a retail worker. Yet six months after the new law passed, these protections have still not come into force.
“Retail workers face abuse every day – their safety must not be the price of government inaction.
“A nationwide week of action against retail crime begins on 9 November, bringing together police, retailers and government in a united effort to tackle offending.
“Ministers should seize the moment to announce the commencement date for these new protections, giving retail workers the reassurance they need and sending a clear message that violence and theft on our streets will not be tolerated.”
Chris Brook-Carter, chief executive of retail industry charity the Retail Trust, said: “The small reduction in retail crime is another sign that combined efforts by the government, police and retailers are starting to make a difference, but there is still much more to do before people working on the frontline of retail feel genuinely safer and happier at work.
“Today’s figures don’t yet the reflect the reality of many of the shop workers we speak to, who tell us their confidence, wellbeing and sense of safety are being damaged by daily incidents of theft, violence and abuse.
“This is at the same time that our latest Retail People Index shows four in 10 staff are at already risk of working while unwell and nearly half are considering leaving their jobs.
“The stronger protections for shop staff being introduced as part of the Crime and Policing Act are also welcome steps towards dealing with persistent offenders and serious crime. But these measures alone won’t bring an end to the everyday hostility, intimidation and verbal abuse that too many shop workers face, and which often goes unreported.
“The improvements we’re seeing in recorded shop theft now need to be backed by consistent enforcement, better reporting processes and more practical training and wellbeing support to help staff respond to and recover from incidents.
“Every one of us also needs to play our part in challenging the attitudes that have allowed abuse towards shop workers to become so commonplace by creating more positive, respectful interactions between customers and retail staff.
“Threats, intimidation and hostility should never be accepted as simply ‘part of the job’, and we hope these figures signal that the tide may finally be beginning to turn after years of unacceptably high levels of crime and abuse so that shop staff can feel genuinely safer, more respected and properly supported.”
Matt Dawes, head of enterprise at bodycam specialist HALOS, commented: “A 2% fall in shoplifting is positive, but the headline crime figures only tell part of the story.
“The stats don’t necessarily reflect how safe retail workers feel on the shop floor or the aggression and intimidation they may face but never formally report.
“Lower retail crime figures need to translate into better experiences for employees too. Staff need to know that when something does happen, there’s a clear process for reporting it and that incidents will be taken seriously.
“Retailers need to focus on training, clear procedures and the right technology to help staff feel protected without placing the burden of intervention on them.
“Falling shoplifting figures are encouraging, but the real measure of progress is whether people on the shop floor feel safe and supported at work.”
ACS highlights increasingly violent shop theft in latest crime figures
Joanne Thomas, Usdaw general secretary, commented: “Retail crime remains at epidemic levels with over half a million shop theft incidents recorded. This is not a victimless crime.
“Dealing with repeated and persistent offences can cause issues beyond the theft itself, like anxiety, fear and physical harm to retail workers on the frontline.
“We have campaigned, along with many retail employers, for substantial legislative measures to combat this growing problem and we are pleased that the Government passed the Crime and Policing Act in April. The Act delivers a much-needed protection of retail workers law, which still needs to be brought into force, and we urge Ministers to do that as soon as possible.
“New Respect Orders for offenders, starting next week, are welcome and we hope they will be successful in changing the criminal behaviour that is blighting our shops and communities.
“The government is rebuilding neighbourhood policing. Every community has named local officers and more than 3,800 additional neighbourhood policing personnel have been delivered. They are targeting the people causing the most harm: prolific offenders, repeat offenders and organised criminal networks.
“It is welcome news that shop theft figures have fallen for the third consecutive quarter. It is our hope that these new measures will help turn the tide on shop theft and give retail staff the safe working environment they deserve.”

items.body:
With the festive season approaching and an unprecedented increase of shoppers flocking to TikTok to search for gift inspiration, brands need to maximise the platform’s growth to drive sales. New research by Bazaarvoice, the platform connecting over 13,000 brands and retailers to authentic shopper content, finds that while 66% of UK consumers now purchase goods on TikTok Shop and one in five use it at least once per week, trust remains a barrier to purchasing through the platform.
TikTok Shop is the fourth largest beauty retailer in the UK according to NielsenIQ. Last month, Boots joined the likes of Sephora and Marks & Spencer to sell their products on the platform, saying it would “bring trusted beauty expertise to a new generation of social shoppers.”
Bazaarvoice’s research shows that three quarters of shoppers have bought a product on TikTok Shop that they wouldn’t have considered buying elsewhere, and almost two thirds (64%) use the platform to discover new brands and trends.
With this in mind, it is easy to see why so many retailers and brands are choosing the social media giant to market their products for sale.
The research delves further into why consumers choose certain products and brands over others. Tellingly, 68% of shoppers are more likely to trust an everyday customer than an influencer when making a purchase on the platform.
When asked about the most important factor in their buying decision, three quarters (74%) of TikTok shoppers said star ratings and customer reviews were most important, followed by 56% who cited customer photos and videos, and just 31% who stated influencer endorsements.
David McIntosh, general manager EMEA at Bazaarvoice said, “TikTok Shop creates a fantastic opportunity for retailers to reach new customers, and this research highlights that whilst shoppers discover products through creators and they look to other customers before they buy, one of the most important elements of the sales process is trust in the brand and product.
“There is a great opportunity now for brands to focus on building authentic relationships with their customers through the use of trusted user generated content, such as customer reviews and ratings, and customer photos and videos. Actions like this could go a long way to turning prospective shoppers into long-term customers.”
Additional findings from the research include:
- 40% of shoppers are triggered to purchase on TikTok Shop by creator content
- 47% of shoppers would be more likely to shop with TikTok Shop than a traditional retailer if there was authentic video proof of the product
- 99% of respondents said they trust customer written reviews, photos and videos when making a decision to purchase

items.body:
Specialist Snowsport retailer Snow+Rock, a brand with Cotswold Outdoor Group, is celebrating raising over £50,000 for youth charity Snow Camp since January 2025. The funds will help 500 young people from inner-city and disadvantaged communities take part in Snow Camp’s First Tracks programme and experience skiing and snowboarding for the very first time.
The funds have been raised through donations from Snow+Rock’s customers, who have been invited to round up their purchases at the checkout to support Snow Camp’s important work with young people.
The programme aims to make snowsports accessible to young people who might otherwise be unable to experience them. Through combining time on the slopes with classroom-based life-skills sessions, Snow Camp’s First Tracks is designed to build confidence, develop essential life skills, and open new opportunities.
Upon completion, participants receive an accredited Snow Life Award. For many, First Tracks marks the start of a longer snowsport journey, with opportunities to progress through Snow Camp’s intermediate and advanced programmes, gain further qualifications, access apprenticeships and explore future careers within the industry.
Sharing their experience, one Snow Camp graduate commented, “Before joining Snow Camp, I wasn’t in a very good place, and I often found it difficult to step outside my comfort zone. Being part of the programme encouraged me to challenge myself, take on new opportunities, and believe in my own abilities. It has helped me become more confident, more motivated, and given me goals to work towards, including becoming a qualified snowboard instructor.”
The partnership reflects Snow+Rock’s commitment to supporting the wider snowsports community. By giving customers a simple way to contribute at checkout, the retailer is helping Snow Camp create opportunities that extend far beyond the slopes.
Jamie Kristow, CEO at Cotswold Outdoor Group said, “We are incredibly proud to have raised over £50,000 for Snow Camp since January 2025, and we are so grateful to our generous customers for making this possible. Our partnership with Snow Camp is hugely valued at Snow+Rock. Together, we are making a positive impact on the snowsports industry and helping to make snowsports more accessible to the next generation.”
Dan Charlish, founder of Snow Camp, added, “When we first discussed what might be possible between Snow Camp and Snow+Rock many years ago, we could never have imagined the partnership evolving to what it is today.
To be where we are now with the Pennies campaign – collecting donations across all Snow+Rock stores – is truly remarkable; changing young lives and laying the foundations for even greater things to come.
On behalf of everyone involved with Snow Camp, we couldn’t be more grateful to the entire Snow+Rock team for their ongoing support.”

items.body:
The Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) has decided that Aldi, Lidl GB and Lidl NI will be designated as ‘Large Grocery Retailers’ (LGRs) under the Groceries Market Investigation (Controlled Land) Order 2010.
The Order has applied to Asda, Co‑op, Marks and Spencer, Morrisons, Sainsbury’s, Tesco and Waitrose since 2010. The Order is designed to stop Large Grocery Retailers from using land agreements to make it harder for rival supermarkets to open nearby – in particular through the use of restrictive covenants and exclusivity arrangements. The rules ensure supermarkets compete freely – and ultimately ensure shoppers have more choice about where to buy, and how much to pay for, their groceries.
In August, the CMA invited views on its proposal to designate Aldi, Lidl GB and Lidl NI under the Order. Interested parties including Morrisons, Waitrose and Iceland submitted their views, and all supported the CMA’s proposal. The CMA did not receive representations from Aldi, Lidl GB or Lidl NI.
Once a retailer is designated, it cannot include any prohibited restrictions in new agreements – and existing agreements can be reviewed by the CMA, on the request of interested landowners, developers, and rival supermarkets. This is the case for all designated supermarkets.
Juliette Enser, executive director for Competition Enforcement and Markets at the CMA, said: “We put in place rules to stop big supermarket chains from blocking rival stores opening in their area, and now those rules apply to Aldi and Lidl.
“This will help level the playing field and make sure shoppers get the best choice of products and prices in their area.”
The UK food and grocery market is worth an estimated £222.7 billion, with Aldi and Lidl ranking among the top 5 retailers by market share.
For more information, read the CMA’s final decisions report and supporting documents on the case page.

The partnership strengthens how Primark tests and validates operational and capital changes before implementation. items.body:
Primark has partnered with Kallikor, the supply chain network design platform, to introduce a simulation-led approach to significant strategic supply chain decisions. The partnership strengthens how Primark tests and validates operational and capital changes before implementation.
The engagement begins with creating digital twins of Primark’s distribution centres, allowing teams to test alternative operating configurations before implementation. By comparing scenarios in a simulated environment, Primark can identify more efficient approaches while protecting customer service and avoiding downstream cost or operational impacts across the store estate.
Adam Hoccom, director of supply chain at Primark, said: “As Primark continues to grow across markets, ensuring our supply chain is designed to support that ambition is critical. A key part of that is making sure our distribution centres operate efficiently while remaining aligned to store needs. Working with Kallikor allows us to test and compare different operating configurations – from layout and flow changes within sites to broader network considerations – before we commit capital spend.
This gives us greater confidence in the choices we make and how they will perform in practice, strengthening our ability to innovate and make well-informed decisions as we evolve our network.”
By modelling operational flows in detail – from pick paths and labour constraints to throughput variability and service impacts – Primark can see how proposed changes will perform in practice before they are introduced. The models are built from Primark’s operational data, ensuring outcomes reflect how the system actually performs under a range of real operating conditions rather than relying on assumptions or averaged views of the network.
The modelling also establishes a living decision environment built on Primark’s operational data that can be reused and extended as new strategic questions arise. Rather than commissioning a new analysis for each decision, teams can continuously test alternatives within the same validated model as the supply chain evolves.
Through simulation and AI-enabled scenario exploration, Primark teams can run and compare multiple operating futures side-by-side – assessing trade-offs across cost, service, capacity and risk in parallel. This ensures that viable options are explored comprehensively and that the strongest strategic path is chosen with clarity and confidence. It also provides a shared, system-wide evidence base that supports confident cross-functional alignment around significant strategic choices.
Jack O’Connell, CEO & co-founder of Kallikor, said: “At Primark’s scale, no supply chain decision exists in isolation. A change in one distribution centre can affect capacity, flow, service and performance across the wider network. Our role is to help teams explore decisions that would otherwise carry too much uncertainty, testing different scenarios before implementation so leaders can understand the trade-offs and move forward with confidence.
We’re proud to support Primark as they build a simulation-led decision-making capability, beginning with their distribution centres and creating the foundations for better decisions across the wider supply chain over time.”
While the initial focus is on distribution centre configuration, the modelling environment is designed to be reused as new questions arise – allowing teams to test automation pathways, capital investments, network design changes and future growth scenarios within the same validated system.
The partnership represents a step toward a more evidence-led approach to supply chain decision-making – ensuring that future growth and investment choices can be tested against operational reality before change is locked in.

items.title: Landsec’s blocked £.5bn shopping centre plan leaves Lewisham in the worst of all worlds
items.summary: Lewisham’s £1.5bn shopping centre redevelopment freeze, caused by a breakdown between Landsec and the Council, has left residents, traders, and the town centre stranded in uncertainty, says Sergiy Lesyk Lewisham shows how a council can lose a £1.5bn scheme and gain nothing. Landsec, the property company that has owned Lewisham Shopping Centre for more than [...]
items.body:
Landsec’s blocked £.5bn shopping centre plan leaves Lewisham in the worst of all worlds
Lewisham’s £1.5bn shopping centre redevelopment freeze, caused by a breakdown between Landsec and the Council, has left residents, traders, and the town centre stranded in uncertainty, says Sergiy Lesyk
Lewisham shows how a council can lose a £1.5bn scheme and gain nothing.
Landsec, the property company that has owned Lewisham Shopping Centre for more than 20 years, has put its £1.5bn redevelopment of the centre on hold. Councillors approved the scheme in October 2025, and work had been due to start in 2027. Now nobody can say when, or whether, anything will happen.
You don’t have to have liked the plans to see the problem that residents and traders in Lewisham now face.
Landsec gave two reasons: one was the cost of building in London, the other was the Council. In Landsec’s words, recent statements from the Council “make clear that the administration is not able to support the next phase of land assembly needed to unlock delivery without a significant increase in affordable housing.”
On a social video, the mayor, Liam Shrivastava, had the temerity to state “the conditions for such developments are simply not favourable right now”, and that “the way out of the housing crisis is through building social housing.”
The mayor was elected on a promise of 1,000 new social rent homes. Instead, the plan to replace the shopping centre with 1,744 homes, including 98 for social rent and 231 at discounted rents or for key workers, will no longer be built. The shopping centre development took about five years to approve, so who really thinks this council will match it any time soon?
Boots has left its high street unit, which sits in the first phase, for a unit inside the centre. Marks & Spencer, a fixture in Lewisham for almost a century, has closed for good, Natwest has said it will close its branch, and the Model Market food hall still hasn’t reopened.
Landsec itself says the 1970s building is no longer fit for purpose, as it had been expected to be demolished.
Labour, which approved the scheme, and the Greens, who now run the Council, are busy blaming each other, and the mayor is blaming the government. Finger-pointing won’t build a single home or fill a single empty unit.
Lewisham is being let down
And the drift goes well beyond the shopping centre. A short walk away, the 649 homes of the Filigree at Lewisham Gateway have stood empty since a flood in February 2025, and residents won’t be back before October 2027. Nearby, one resident told us that food waste bins turned up at their block with no guidance and no collections. The building manager has had to tell everyone not to use them until the council explains what happens next. Even the council’s own website can’t seem to agree on whether flats are getting food waste collections.
This matters well beyond SE13. London needs homes, and it needs investors with the long-term support and confidence of local councils to build them.
So what should happen now?
First, the council should be straight with residents about what it told Landsec and what it now expects to happen to the site.
Second, it should publish a support plan for the traders caught up in the uncertainty, because they’re paying for decisions they didn’t make.
Third, and most importantly, it should set out its own plan for Lewisham town centre. If this scheme wasn’t good enough, the Council needs to show what would be, who will build it, and when.
Lewisham Conservatives support homes and investment in Lewisham, but not a town centre left in limbo. Residents were promised new homes, a new town centre and a new community. They’ve been let down. The council can’t build any of it until it first rebuilds their trust.
Sergiy Lesyk is chairman of Lewisham Conservatives

Today the grocer has also announced the acquisition of four new sites which […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
Waitrose today opens a brand-new 18,000sq ft ‘Home of Food Lovers’ store in Cricklewood, North West London – the grocer’s first full line supermarket opening in eight years.
The next Waitrose supermarket opening will be in Hale Barns, Greater Manchester, this November.
Today the grocer has also announced the acquisition of four new sites which underpin its approach to having the right store in the right location. Joining the two new supermarkets will be a new neighbourhood store in Oakham (Rutland) and three new convenience stores in Bedminster (Bristol), Chalk Farm (London) and Springstead Village (Cambridge) which will open from 2027.
Waitrose operates three main types of store with the size, layout and ranging tailored to local needs. Small convenience stores in busy urban areas focus on fresh top-up items and quick, on-the-go purchases. Mid-size ‘neighbourhood’ stores in suburban areas carry over 6,500 products, making them ideal for everything from quick drop-ins to weekly shops. Larger supermarkets serve as destination stores with room to showcase the full breadth of the Waitrose range and concepts.
The announcements form part of Waitrose’s £1 billion multi-year investment plan, which includes expansion, store updates and the growth of its online and wholesale channels, to provide the best experience for customers.
Waitrose Cricklewood
The Cricklewood shop marks the next phase in rolling out Waitrose’s ‘Home of Food Lovers’ concept – first trialled in Newbury and now serving as the blueprint for new openings and refurbishments, adapted to suit each local community.
Central to the offering is Waitrose’s approach to quality, food integrity and animal welfare. Key features include dedicated meat, fish and sushi counters, dry-aged beef cabinet, hand-cut and speciality cheeses, on-site bakery, Fine & Rare wine selection and a fruit and veg section championing organic, Fairtrade, and regeneratively-farmed produce.
Behind the experience is a team of Partners who’ve completed extensive training to help customers discover what’s on offer. Partners in Beers, Wines & Spirits, Bakery and Counters have also completed additional training and qualifications through organisations including the Wine & Spirit Education Trust, Guild of Fine Food and specialist suppliers such as Dovecote Park and Pilgrims.
The team includes 69 new Partners who join 53 experienced team members as co-owners in the John Lewis Partnership. Three appointments were made through the Partnership’s Building Happier Futures programme, which delivers tailored support, job shadowing, and long-term career pathways for care-experienced young people.
Tina Mitchell, Waitrose retail director, said: “Our supermarkets provide the ultimate showcase for everything that sets Waitrose apart – from our unmatched quality and industry-leading welfare standards to the expert service of our Partners.
“Opening Cricklewood as our first new full-line supermarket in eight years marks an important step in bringing Waitrose closer to more communities. We continue to invest in the right shops in the right locations alongside delivering the experience customers expect from Waitrose through our online offering and wider network.”
Nationwide investment
Waitrose’s investment programme includes 29 store refurbishments this year alone and alongside today’s four new store announcements, the grocer continues work on previously announced sites – a convenience store in Ascot (Berkshire) and a 30,000 sq ft shop in Brabazon (Bristol).
To support existing stores and unlock further growth, Waitrose will open its first South West distribution centre in Avonmouth early next year.

items.title: Christmas food price rises won't be as bad as feared, says Sainsbury's boss
items.summary: The boss of Sainsbury's has said consumers will be spared dramatic price rises this Christmas but reiterated calls for the Government to relieve pressure on businesses.
items.body:
Christmas food price rises won't be as bad as feared, says Sainsbury's boss
The boss of Sainsbury's has said consumers will be spared dramatic price rises this Christmas but reiterated calls for the Government to relieve pressure on businesses.
Simon Roberts said food inflation had not 'moved anything like' the dire levels predicted by the wider industry in the immediate outbreak of the Middle East conflict.
The Food and Drink Federation's forecasts saw food inflation topping 9 per cent by the end of the year, but prices were unchanged at 1.3 per cent in the year to September, according to figures from the Office for National Statistics.
But the supermarket boss urged the Government to keep pressures on the cost of food and employment down.
In a pre-Budget plea, Roberts urged the Chancellor to use next week’s Budget to support businesses instead of ‘adding further taxes or further regulatory impacts to an industry that’s already very heavily taxed.’
Sainsbury's Simon Roberts said food inflation had not reached anywhere near levels predicted by industry gr
He said that the shock increase in National Insurance contributions had increased costs in the retail and hospitality sectors and the Government should ‘make sure we don't do anything to further aggravate that situation.’
Defending reports of supermarkets’ pleas to be excluded from high business rates, Roberts said that retail is ‘one of the highest taxed sectors’ and includes major employers which employ millions of people.
The Chancellor last week met with bosses from Morrisons, Sainsbury's and Tesco, where Roberts said he felt 'heard'.
The remarks from the chief executive came as Britain’s second biggest grocer upgraded its annual profit forecasts and said customers will not ‘trade down’ this Christmas despite economic pressures.
The group had been forecasting profits between £965 million and £1.065 billion but raised this to a range between £1.025 billion and £1.065billion - after the impact of the war in the Middle East had taken less of a toll than feared.
The grocer said booming sales of its own-label premium Taste The Difference ranges helped grocery sales rise 2.9 per cent to £13.2 billion.
Customers were ‘planning early’ for the festive season, with Sainsbury's adding more online grocery shops to keep up with demand.
Roberts added: ‘I think [what] will be a real theme into Christmas, is customers don't want to trade down. They want the best value and the best quality, and that's really what we are focused on.’
There had been ‘a lot of concern earlier in the year as to where food inflation might go,’ Roberts said, but ‘actually [it] has yet to see much of a move’.
But he said there was ‘pressure’ in the system heading into the autumn and winter, including fertiliser prices and energy costs. ‘We’re going to be doing what we’ve done consistently, working really hard to give customers the value that they expect,’ he said.
But shares tumbled 3 per cent after Sainsbury's revealed slower sales growth.
Lucy Rumbold, equity research analyst at Quilter, said: 'It’s worth noting that inflationary pressures stemming from developments in the Middle East have taken longer than initially expected to feed across European markets.
'Grocers such as Sainsbury’s have therefore kept price growth below headline inflation to protect their value proposition, which has seemingly weighed on like-for-like sales. However, this as a sensible strategy.
'If Sainsbury’s continues to resonate with households on value for money, it should be well positioned to benefit as inflation is eventually passed through. We expect this to become more evident towards year-end, as higher fertiliser costs feed through and lower-cost inventory is depleted.'

items.body:
John Lewis launches its biggest-ever fashion collaboration, bringing iconic British brand RIXO to 30 John Lewis stores, further strengthening its premium fashion credentials. Launching 22nd October, John Lewis x RIXO is a vintage-inspired collection rooted in a shared belief that clothes should make you feel like the best version of yourself. Distinctly RIXO in spirit, each piece has been designed to be worn again and again; styled uniquely to the wearer, suited to any occasion, and timeless enough to never go out of style.
On the collection, RIXO Co-Founder Orlagh McCloskey says: “This collaboration feels like a true extension of RIXO – taking the heritage of John Lewis, leaning into its incredible archive, and bringing it to life with that RIXO magic.
“For me, if you’re going to do a collaboration, you have to do it properly. It should feel as strong, if not stronger, than anything you’ve created before – every piece considered, every detail cared for, and something you feel genuinely proud to put your name to.
“We wanted the collection to do the talking. We can’t wait to see women across the UK, whether they’re longtime RIXO lovers or discovering us for the first time through John Lewis, style it in their own way and make it theirs.
“We feel incredibly proud to have created something that reaches a wider audience than our London stores.”
Celebrating design heritage and authenticity, the collection features an exclusive floral motif inspired by a block-printed textile from 1849, thoughtfully selected from The JLP Archive during the collaborative design process. This is the first time an archive print has been used in a John Lewis fashion collaboration. The signature print features across two dresses, a blouse, skirt and scarf.
The collection includes dresses, knitwear, blouses, jackets, skirts, scarves, shoes and bags, bringing together the design ethos of both brands, where signature RIXO silhouettes meet John Lewis wearability. New shapes and patterns offer something truly unique and special, available exclusively at John Lewis. Among them, is the hero piece The Vesper: a full-length dress finished with delicate cap sleeves and a ruffle neckline, in the aforementioned archive print.
Flattering silhouettes meet considered design details to create pieces that customers will reach for time and time again. Vintage floral prints in an autumnal palette feature throughout alongside luxe velvets, decadent sequins, soft cashmere and silky lamé. Fur and lace trims, ruffles, metallic embroidery and intricate embellishments make each piece feel extra special.
Heroes from the collection include the Luanne fur trimmed jacquard jacket, the Carina lace and archive print dress and the Delphina mini dress in a bold floral print. Accessories complete the collection with a distinctively vintage feel, think intricate beaded bags, silky scarves and statement metallic footwear.
Rachel Morgans, fashion director at John Lewis, says: “RIXO is an iconic British brand adored by so many, much like John Lewis, so it felt natural to create something special together. RIXO has such a strong community so we feel honoured to be a part of it and we’re proud to be supporting a British, female-founded brand. Being able to use the John Lewis Partnership Archive for the collection feels extra special, using our extensive heritage to create something that feels contemporary and unique for our customers.”
The collection will be available in all John Lewis fashion stores and on johnlewis.com. Prices range from £65 for a scarf – £525 for a lace trimmed dress. Selected mainline RIXO jewellery and footwear featured in the campaign will also be available online from 22 October.

items.title: Met Police rogue store crackdown results in closures and arrests across London
items.summary: The fight against rogue retailers across London has led to the arrest of 42 people and closure notices issued for 11 shops, during a two-week crackdown on the resale of stolen goods. Around 400 shops suspected of buying and reselling stolen goods were visited by… This story continues at Met Police rogue store crackdown results in closures and arrests across London Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
Around 400 shops suspected of buying and reselling stolen goods were visited by officers from the Met as part of the operation.
From food products to expensive cosmetics and electrical goods, tens of thousands of pounds worth of suspected stolen stock were seized.
Ahead of the operation, months of joint work between the Met, retailers and Trading Standards helped identify rogue businesses suspected of buying and selling stolen goods.
Retailers also highlighted the products most frequently targeted by thieves. These items were marked with SelectaDNA, a forensic marking solution that leaves a unique traceable code, identifiable under UV light.
This enables officers to link recovered goods directly back to the stores they were stolen from.
Intelligence shows that prolific shoplifters are stealing to order from high street retailers, targeting specific products requested by those buying and reselling stolen goods.
These ‘shopping lists’ help fuel the organised criminal supply chain.
As millions of Londoners and visitors head to the capital’s world class stores, shopping centres and local businesses for their Christmas shopping, the mayor and Met police promised to continue working closely with retail leads and partners to prevent shoplifting, catch criminals and make the capital even safer.
Deputy commissioner Matt Jukes said: “Honest retailers have been clear that they want action against the minority of rogue businesses that fuel retail crime, undercut legitimate traders and damage confidence in our high streets.
“This Met operation has done exactly that, targeting those who create a market for stolen goods and profit from criminality.
“Over the last two weeks, Met officers have targeted every stage of the criminal chain, from prolific shoplifters stealing to order through to the shop owners buying and reselling stolen goods.
“Tens of thousands of pounds worth of suspected stolen goods have been seized, shop owners arrested and businesses closed down.
“Those results send a clear message: if you profit from retail crime, you will be arrested. “Working alongside partners such as retailers and Trading Standards, we will use every power available to disrupt this criminality, protect honest businesses and make London’s high streets safer.”
For the first time, the Met has also issued warning notices to car boot sale organisers, making clear they could face criminal liability if they knowingly facilitate or ignore the sale of stolen, counterfeit and illicit goods at their events.
During the rest of the two-week deployment:
- Whilst conducting a licensing check at a shop in Lewisham on Monday, 19 October, officers identified suspected stolen Tesco tinned mackerel being sold. Further searches led to the recovery of a machete as well as suspected stolen passports and driving licences being stored in a sweet tin. Two suspects were arrested for offences including handling stolen goods and possession of offensive weapon.
- Two arrests were made following a licensing check at a retail premises in Clapham, on Sunday, 19 October. Officers recovered branded meat products from Sainsbury, Coop and Iceland to the value of £1,000, two knives and large quantity of Class B drugs.
- £15,000 in cash and 300 suspected stolen mobile phones were seized following a warrant executed alongside Trading Standards in Hounslow on Monday, 12 October. Two men were arrested on suspicion of handling stolen goods, and a three-month closure order was granted for the store.
- Dozens of suspected stolen mobile phones and more than £5,000 in cash were seized during a warrant at a mobile phone shop in Brixton on Monday, 19 October. Three men were arrested on suspicion of handling stolen goods and money laundering.
- 10 bottles of Boots suncream and three bottles of M&S wine were recovered during a licensing check at a store in Southall on Monday, 12 October. One woman was arrested on suspicion of handling stolen goods.
The mayor of London, Sadiq Khan, said: “Shoplifting is not a victimless crime. The lead up to Christmas is vital to London’s economy and we must do everything we can to prevent criminals exploiting busy shopping periods and inflicting so much misery on our hardworking business owners and staff.
“That’s why the Met is stepping up action against the most prolific offenders, using new technology to link offences across stores and locations, identify repeat offenders and build stronger cases for prosecution.
“Thanks to intensified action by the Met and its partners, the number of shoplifting offences being solved has doubled, leading to 1,800 additional arrests. But there is more to do, and I will continue working with the police, retailers and local partners to make London a no-go zone for shoplifters and build a safer city for everyone.”
This operation is part of the Met’s continued work to tackle retail crime. Across London in 2025, shoplifting fell by 3.7 per cent, around 3,500 fewer offences, while positive outcomes for shoplifting investigations doubled.
Investment in new retail crime reporting technology has strengthened efforts to identify and target prolific offenders. In boroughs where the system has been introduced, positive outcomes have quadrupled this year.
Tesco UK shrink and security director, Rachel Bennett, said: “As one of the UK’s largest retailers, we see first-hand the impact retail crime can have on colleagues, customers and the communities we serve. Tesco has been at the forefront of efforts to tackle the issue, working alongside the Metropolitan Police and other partners to improve reporting, share intelligence and support enforcement action.
“This operation is a powerful example of what can be achieved through that collaboration, helping to drive retail crime out of communities and creating safer environments for everyone.”
Association of Convenience Stores (ACS) chief executive, Ed Woodall, said: “We fully support the Met’s efforts to shut down those selling stolen goods in the capital, and need to continue disrupting the illicit networks that steal from legitimate retailers, prop up dodgy shops, and engage in a long list of other criminal activity.
“Responsible local shops remain committed to doing their part by investing thousands in each store on crime prevention and detection measures to ensure the police have the evidence they need to take action.”
Director of UK sales & business development at SelectaDNA, Clair Frame, said: “Operation Zoridon continues to go from strength to strength, and its success comes down to collaboration.
“Retailers share what they’re seeing on the shop floor, officers turn that into targeted action, and we support both with deployment of SelectaDNA solutions to mark stock, which is vulnerable to theft, as well as detection through the use of our SelectaDNA search dog.
“This joint approach has delivered positive results, both in disrupting the outlets that handle stolen goods and in rebuilding retailers’ confidence that reporting and sharing actionable intelligence makes a difference.
“We’re proud to be part of it and keen to work with more retailers nationally to bring the same approach to communities across the UK.”

Sainsbury’s shares slide as ‘tough’ conditions slow growth
Shares in Sainsbury’s tumbled after the supermarket giant posted slowing sales growth and warned that shoppers are facing “tough” cost-of-living pressures.
The UK’s second-largest supermarket saw its stock slide by nearly four per cent in early trading to 346p. This came despite the firm lifting the lower end of its full-year profit target from £965m to £1.025bn, with an upper range of £1.065bn.
The FTSE 100 firm’s like-for-like sales growth slowed in the three months to September, from 2.3 to 1.2 per cent. Grocery sales growth slowed from 3.5 to 2.2 per cent while general merchandise and clothing sales improved slightly, from a decrease of 3.7 to 2.9 per cent.
Sainsbury’s chief executive Simon Roberts conceded that the supermarket chain’s volume growth “has been a bit subdued through this period”. But he added that, “given the strength of our performance in the previous summer, we’re actually pretty encouraged by the performance we’ve seen”.
Since taking the reins as boss in 2020, Roberts has pushed for the grocer to focus more on its food offering. In July, Sainsbury’s sold Argos – the struggling general retailer it owns – to Swift Partners for £120m.
The impact of this sale on Sainsbury’s’ balance sheet pushed the firm to pre-tax loss of £164m in the first half of the year, though its underlying pre-tax profit improved by five per cent to £366m.
Roberts told shareholders on Thursday that the disposal of Argos will help to create a “simpler, more focused Sainsbury’s”. The grocery boss said demand for its up-market Taste the Difference range is driving its growth in food.
Sales in this category grew by more than six per cent in the second quarter. The supermarket’s “restaurant-quality” Taste the Difference Discovery Range – which sits at an even higher price point and includes BBQ and Italian offerings – will soon reach 200 products, Roberts said.
Sainsbury’s walks away from Morrisons talks
Demand for up-market food is growing despite reports of plummeting consumer confidence. Roberts said: “We know many households are finding things tough at the moment and we’re making it easier for customers to enjoy good food every day, whatever their budget.
“That’s why more people are choosing us for their weekly shop, driving continued volume growth in the first half.”
Surging energy and supply costs caused by the Iran war are set to push food inflation beyond six per cent by July next year, but supermarket bosses have so far refused to say whether the conflict is putting pressure on their prices.
Tesco boss Ken Murphy has said he doesn’t recognise industry inflation forecasts while Murphy said earlier this year that grocery price rises have not been as bad as feared.
Sainsbury’s market share slipped from 15.3 to 15.2 per cent in the year to October, according to Worldpanel data, leaving it behind market leader Tesco, on 27.8 per cent.
The supermarket’s attempts to gain on its rival were thrown into the spotlight earlier this month when it emerged that it had held merger talks with smaller rival Morrisons.
The supermarket walked away from discussions in February following a disagreement over price but the revelation was taken by many in the retail sector to signal the start of a fresh wave of consolidation among the UK’s retailers.

items.title: Sensei looks to take retail intelligence beyond the store checkout as it teams with Brazil’s Muffato Group
items.summary: Sensei has deployed its technology in a new Muffato Go store in Curitiba, Brazil. This has been developed in partnership with supermarket specialist Grupo Muffato.While Sensei first became known for its autonomous store technology, it says that the intelligence behind those stores has always been de
items.body:
Sensei has deployed its technology in a new Muffato Go store in Curitiba, Brazil. This has been developed in partnership with supermarket specialist Grupo Muffato.
While Sensei first became known for its autonomous store technology, it says that the intelligence behind those stores has always been designed to address a broader challenge: giving physical retail the ability and the data to understand and automate its own operations in real-time.
The new Muffato Go, according to those involved, will put that capability into practice, showing how the same underlying technology can improve shelf availability, detect losses, automate checkout, manage fresh products and support online order fulfillment.
Headquartered in Portugal and operating across Europe and Brazil, Sensei has deployed its technology in more than 100 autonomous points of sale, including the world's largest autonomous store, opened in Leiria, Portugal, in 2025.
“The new Muffato Go shows what AI can already do in a physical store. Shoppers get a faster, simpler way to buy, but that is only the visible part. Our models recognise products and shopper interactions as they happen, and store teams get the right task at the right time," says Vasco Portugal, CEO and Co-founder at Sensei.
"The real value is turning what happens in the store into intelligence that supports the entire business, from the shop floor to the head office. That is what we mean by Conscious Spaces: physical spaces that see, understand and act."
Combining computer vision, deep learning, neural networks and sensor fusion, Sensei’s technology recognises products and pseudonymised customer interactions, builds virtual shopping baskets and enables customers to complete purchases without scanning items individually, by associating the items to a token that represents the customer at the checkout.
“Innovation and the willingness to take bold steps are part of who we are. We are committed to making retail increasingly efficient, and the new generation of MGO reflects that ambition: using technology to enhance the shopping experience. With four years of work together with Sensei, that same technology now gives us a clearer view of how the store operates, from the shelf to the checkout,” says Everton Muffato, Director at Grupo Muffato.
Advances in AI integrated technology also allow the system to handle variable weight products, extending the experience to fresh produce and bakery items. Beyond the customer journey, the same intelligence alerts store teams when products need replenishing, helps identify losses in real-time, and provides more accurate information to support stock management, store layout and online order preparation."
The partnership between Sensei and Grupo Muffato began in 2022, with the Muffato Go concept in Curitiba, Sensei’s first deployment outside Europe. Four years later, Grupo Muffato is looking to turn Muffato Go into a new business model for the group, and the new store, which it labels the largest autonomous store in Latin America, marks the next step in that push.

items.body:
Kevel has pulled in $52 million in funding, marking the largest capital raise in the company’s history.
The financing includes expanded investments from Fulcrum Equity Partners, dunnhumby Ventures, Iberis Capital and additional growth capital from ORIX Corporation USA’s Growth Capital business.
Kevel’s total capital raised now exceeds $100 million. The retail media technology specialist works with the likes of Tesco, Dollar General Media Networks, John Lewis Partnership, Paypal, Scandinavian Airlines, Home Depot’s Orange Apron Media, and Nubank, across North America, Europe, LATAM, and APAC.
“Commerce media is entering a new era, one defined by ownership, transparency, and AI driven infrastructure built around the business rather than intermediaries,” says James Avery, Founder and CEO at Kevel.
“To keep commerce media open and competitive, businesses must own their monetisation and data. This raise enables us to scale the technology retailers and marketplaces need to build differentiated media networks, drive sustainable growth, and compete head to head with the largest platforms."
“Kevel has built an impressive, highly differentiated platform that enables customers to rapidly launch and scale retail media businesses tailored to their unique brands and audiences,” says Blake Zhang, Managing Director in ORIX USA’s Growth Capital business.
“As the market continues to expand across on-site, off-site, in-store and other emerging channels, we believe Kevel is well positioned to help customers navigate that growing complexity and scale across an increasingly broad ecosystem. We are excited to partner with James and the Kevel team as they continue to innovate and help shape the next generation of retail media.”
“Kevel’s continued investment in building cutting-edge infrastructure and AI to power commerce media networks is truly incredible,” comments Philip Lewis, Partner, Fulcrum Equity Partners. “We are thrilled to continue investing to ensure that Kevel has the resources to support the complex needs of our partners.”
The funding will be used for Kevel’s next stage of growth, with AI at the centre of its product roadmap. The company will continue developing its AI decisioning and optimisation capabilities so that every ranking, bid and placement decision is explainable, auditable and configurable by retailers. It says it will also expand globally into new retail and commerce media categories and deepen its strategic advisory services.

items.title: No order, no seat: Starbucks China rolls out new store policy
items.summary: Starbucks says it is improving customers' in-store experience as it competes with homegrown rivals.
items.body:
No order, no seat: Starbucks China rolls out new store policy
- Published
Taking a seat at a Starbucks in China? Just make sure you're also ordering something there.
A new policy by Starbucks China takes effect across all its 8,000 stores on Thursday, making it mandatory for people to purchase items if they want to sit in its cafes.
Starbucks China said the move was part of efforts to improve the "in-store experience" for customers. The company is facing stiff competition from homegrown brands such as Luckin Coffee.
Starbucks stores around the world have also been wrestling with non-paying seat-hoggers and other undesirable behaviour from customers.
In South Korea, Starbucks has told customers to stop bringing "bulky items" into their stores, after some patrons reportedly hogged seats with printers and desktop computers in tow.
In North America, Starbucks reversed its open-door policy which for years allowed people to use their seats and toilets without buying anything, saying that it wanted to "prioritise" paying customers.
Starbucks China is now following suit.
Ahead of the official announcement on Wednesday, reports of the new seating policy at China's Starbucks stores had been circulating this week - along with social media videos of what appear to be "purchase to sit" signs in Starbucks stores.
Many on Chinese social media welcomed the new policy.
"Finally, there won't be peak periods where people are just sitting there not ordering anything, drinking Luckin coffee, playing games and yelling on the phone," reads one of the top-liked comment on Weibo. "Every time I walk around, there's nowhere to sit,"
"There's nothing wrong with it. I'd feel awkward sitting there if I didn't make a purchase. I'd rather leave the seats for those who made purchases and need the seats," another Weibo user commented.
Last month, a Starbucks store in Sichuan province sparked debate after video of its chained-up outdoor seats and tables were circulated on social media. It appeared to be an attempt to block people from sitting there without paying.
Since opening its first store there in 1999, China has become Starbucks' second-largest market. But it has faced stiff competition in recent years from Luckin and other local brands that offer cheaper products.
Luckin also offers a robust app-based ordering system that prioritises grab-and-go transactions, challenging Starbucks' model of a full cafe experience where people can sit down and enjoy their food and drinks.
In 2023, Luckin overtook Starbucks as China's largest coffee chain.
Starbucks said last year it would sell 60% stake of its business in China as part of a $4bn (Â£3.04bn) deal with investment firm Boyu Capital.
In another statement on Wednesday, Starbucks China said it was planning to increase staffing and improve digital systems at its stores, among other investments to "ensure customers receive timely and warm service even during peak hours".

items.summary: Grocer launches Cricklewood store as part of £1bn investment plan, with Hale Barns, Greater Manchester, to follow next month As part of a £1bn investment plan , Waitrose has chosen Cricklewood in north London as the location for its first supermarket in eight years. The upmarket grocer will open the store on Thursday and another supermarket in Hale Barns, Greater Manchester, next month. It also plans four smaller stores next year, including a supermarket in Oakham, Rutland, and three convenience stores in Bedminster (Bristol), Chalk Farm (London) and Springstead Village (Cambridge). Continue reading...
items.body:
As part of a £1bn investment plan, Waitrose has chosen Cricklewood in north London as the location for its first supermarket in eight years.
The upmarket grocer will open the store on Thursday and another supermarket in Hale Barns, Greater Manchester, next month. It also plans four smaller stores next year, including a supermarket in Oakham, Rutland, and three convenience stores in Bedminster (Bristol), Chalk Farm (London) and Springstead Village (Cambridge).
In 2024, Waitrose, which has more than 300 supermarkets, said it planned to open up to four large supermarkets and 100 convenience stores over five years and would also refurbish a number of outlets introducing meat, fish and sushi counters, on-site bakeries and fine wine sections.
Tina Mitchell, the retail director at Waitrose, said: “Our supermarkets provide the ultimate showcase for everything that sets Waitrose apart – from our unmatched quality and industry-leading welfare standards to the expert service of our partners.”
This year the company – led since January by the former Tesco executive Tom Denyard - also plans to refurbish 29 stores.
After a difficult period, when sales were hit by IT problems which led to gaps on shelves, Waitrose is holding market share, according to the latest figures from market analysts Worldpanel by Numerator. However, the chain is coming under pressure from Marks & Spencer, which now has a higher share of the grocery market, under some measures, after opening a number of new food-led outlets.
Sales at Waitrose rose 4% in the six months to 1 August. However, its underlying operating profit slid by £7m to £103m as it invested in keeping prices down and improving its loyalty scheme. It was also hit by higher energy costs during the summer heat wave.
Waitrose’s parent company, the John Lewis Partnership – which is owned by its staff – reported a £98m pre-tax loss in the half-year to 1 August, as sales fell at the department stores despite heavy investment in updating the outlets.
The company has been reducing the number of staff it employs directly as it tries to trim costs.
On Wednesday, the partnership announced it had signed its first company-wide union recognition deal. The collective agreement with Usdaw, the shopworkers’ union, comes ahead of new rights of union access in workplaces that come into force at the end of this month.
Joanne Thomas, the general secretary of Usdaw, said: “Usdaw already has members working within the business and this agreement will strengthen that presence and help us in supporting and representing members across the partnership. We now look forward to growing our membership and influence within the partnership and to working with the partnership’s management on finalising the details of how the agreement will work in practice.”

items.summary: John Healey has been urged to tackle the “tsunami of costs” facing firms as consumer confidence tumbled ahead of the crucial Budget next week. Brits’ confidence in the state of the economy worsened from -32 to -40 in October, according to the British Retail Consortium (BRC)’s index, marking the third consecutive month of deteriorating sentiment.  [...]
items.body:
Budget 2026: Consumer confidence tumbles as Healey urged to slow ‘tsunami of costs’
John Healey has been urged to tackle the “tsunami of costs” facing firms as consumer confidence tumbled ahead of the crucial Budget next week.
Brits’ confidence in the state of the economy worsened from -32 to -40 in October, according to the British Retail Consortium (BRC)’s index, marking the third consecutive month of deteriorating sentiment.
Growing fears of inflation and rising interest rates are combining to worsen consumer attitudes ahead of the Chancellor’s first budget, prompting businesses to warn that they cannot encourage spending any more without tax cuts.
Consumers’ net expectation of the state of their personal finances over the next three months worsened from -15 to -18 this month – the second-lowest level on record.
Brits’ spending expectations rose sharply in October, from a net reading of five to 15. Consumers would have already planned to spend more during the run-up to Christmas but rising inflation has worsened this outlook, the BRC said.
Consumer price inflation leapt from 3.1 to 3.5 per cent in the year to September, marking a worse rise than economists had predicted, it was revealed on Wednesday.
More than a third (36 per cent) of shoppers expect to spend more on groceries in the next three months, compared to 28 per cent in September, indicating that Brits are bracing for the price of food to rise sharply.
Supermarket bosses say they are doing everything they can to keep a lid on rising energy and supply costs, but industry figures have tipped food inflation to surge to 6.4 per cent by July next year.
Healey urged to boost consumer confidence
Helen Dickinson, the BRC’s chief executive, said: “Households everywhere will be looking to the Chancellor to tackle the cost of living challenge at next week’s Budget.
“[The] government must act on the tsunami of costs that have hit the industry, from employer National Insurance Contributions to business rates. A little breathing room for retailers at the Budget can mean a lot of breathing room for households.”
Retailers are “doing everything they can” to keep prices down, Dickinson added, but a 20 per cent jump in tax on the industry across two years has left businesses with “no more room for manoeuvre”.
In recent weeks, retail bosses have urged the government to exclude high street shops from the highest business rates multiplier and roll back recent hikes to employer national insurance contributions (NICs).
Retailers say the NICs increases, along with above-inflation hikes to minimum wage, are preventing them from investing in employment to stem the rising number of young people who are not in education, employment, or training (Neet).
Thierry Garnier, chief executive of B&Q owner Kingfisher, wrote in City AM last week that the company’s provision of work experience placements for young people “depends on what the Chancellor decides in this Budget”.

items.body:
From simple food swaps to a new smoothie hitting supermarket shelves, an expert shares how to give your daily fibre intake a boost
Protein might have been having its moment, but there’s another nutrient you might want to pay attention to: fibre.
According to the National Diet and Nutrition Survey, around 95% of adults in the UK aren’t getting enough of it. The good news? You don’t need to completely overhaul your diet or spend hours meal-prepping to get more fibre into your day.
To help make things easier, Naked Smoothies has teamed up with health expert Dr Emily Jackman to share four simple ways to up your fibre intake, from making smarter supermarket swaps to getting a little more creative in the kitchen.
There’s also a new drink joining the line-up: Naked Fibre Machine, a supercharged smoothie designed to help you get more fibre into your daily routine.
Here’s what you need to know.
1. Find out how much fibre you’re actually getting
First things first: do you know how much fibre you’re eating each day?
Adults are generally advised to aim for around 30g of fibre daily, but the average intake in the UK is closer to 20g.
That’s a pretty big gap, but Dr Jackman says one of the easiest ways to start closing it is by getting familiar with the nutritional information on your favourite foods.
“You don’t need to count every gram but checking labels now and then can help you get a feel for where you could add a little more. Look out for “high fibre”, which means at least 6g per 100g or 3g per 100 kcal. It’s about getting familiar with your usual foods, rather than turning every meal into a maths exercise.”
And if you’re looking for a convenient way to give your intake a boost, Naked Smoothies has launched its new Naked Fibre Machine drink.
Made with real fruit juice, including kiwi and apple, alongside spinach and apple cider vinegar, the smoothie is also suitable for vegans and contains chicory inulin, a source of fibre derived from chicory root.
Available in 300ml and 750ml bottles from Boots, Tesco, Ocado and Sainsbury’s nationwide, it provides 4.2g of fibre per 150ml serving.
2. Give your favourite foods a fibre upgrade
Getting more fibre doesn’t mean you have to ditch all the foods you love.
In fact, some of the easiest ways to increase your intake involve adding a few more ingredients to meals you’re already eating.
Dr Jackman recommends incorporating more fruit and vegetables, beans, lentils, wholegrains, nuts and seeds into your diet.
“Fruit and veg, beans, lentils, wholegrains, nuts and seeds all contribute to your fibre intake. And there are lots of ways to enjoy them. Think colourful salads, chunky soups or a smoothie alongside breakfast. Start with what you like, then try adding a little more variety, whilst keeping an eye on cooking and prep instructions. Frozen fruit and veg count too, so keeping a few favourites in the freezer can make this easier.”
3. Make a few simple swaps
If the thought of completely changing your diet sounds like too much effort, don’t panic.
According to Dr Jackman, small swaps can make a difference, and breakfast is an easy place to start.
“Getting more fibre doesn’t have to mean changing everything you eat. Breakfast is a good place to start: stir chia seeds or ground flaxseed into porridge or yoghurt, or top with berries. Raspberries and blackberries are particularly good sources of fibre. Small additions can become easy everyday habits.”
4. Don’t go from zero to fibre hero overnight
While increasing your fibre intake is a good goal, there’s one thing to bear in mind: going too hard, too quickly can leave you feeling bloated and uncomfortable.
Dr Jackman recommends building up gradually, making one change at a time over a few weeks rather than attempting a complete dietary overhaul overnight.
“Adding lots of fibre at once can leave you feeling bloated and uncomfortable, so build up gradually over a few weeks. Spread fibre-rich foods across your meals and drink plenty of water to help keep things moving. Give your body time to adjust.”
And if you’re after another convenient option, Naked Fibre Machine is available now from Boots, Tesco, Ocado and Sainsbury’s nationwide and comes in a 300ml single-serve bottle for £3 and a 750ml take-home pack priced at £4.50.

items.title: TG Jones owner Modella pulls out of race to buy Poundland
items.summary: TG Jones owner Modella Capital has pulled out of the race to buy Poundland but will still look to pick up some of its stores if a sale process collapses, City AM can reveal. The private equity firm, which also owns Flying Tiger, had expressed an interest in bidding for the entirety of Poundland but [...]
items.body:
TG Jones owner Modella pulls out of race to buy Poundland
TG Jones owner Modella Capital has pulled out of the race to buy Poundland but will still look to pick up some of its stores if a sale process collapses, City AM can reveal.
The private equity firm, which also owns Flying Tiger, had expressed an interest in bidding for the entirety of Poundland but has since withdrawn its interest, sources said.
The investment firm may still join the battle to pick up individual Poundland stores should the company be broken up by its owners, Gordon Brothers, the sources added.
Poundland’s owners are still hoping to find a buyer for the budget chain but retail union Usdaw warned last week the company is teetering on the brink of collapse. The sale process is being run by advisors at Alvarez & Marsal.
Between six and eight retailers have tabled formal bids to buy just some of Poundland’s stores, with these offers ranging from hundreds to just a few of its locations, sources close to the sale said.
A number of high street firms are waiting in the wings to swoop in on their preferred Poundland locations if a break-up of the budget retailer becomes the only option for Gordon Brothers.
Poundland hopes for rush sale
Discount grocer Lidl has tabled a bid for one store in the hopes of picking up several more in the event of a break-up, City AM revealed last week.
Budget supermarket Iceland is also interested in buying a limited number of Poundland stores in the event the troubled retailer’s owners cannot find a single buyer.
Grocery buyers are likely to be interested in the location of Poundland’s stores rather than the stock of the company, analysts have said, with retail firms racing for high quality space on high streets.
Other retailers including B&M, The Range and Poundstretcher – Poundland’s American rival – are interested in snapping up varying numbers of shops if the company is split apart.
Martin Property Group, the Irish firm which recently bought National Car Parks (NCP) out of administration, is Poundland’s preferred bidder among those who want to acquire the entire business.
Three merger and acquisition (M&A) experts were parachuted onto Poundland’s board last week to reassure other bidders that the process would be run fairly, after managing director Barry Williams and finance chief Shaun Wills endorsed Martin’s bid.
Andrew Kirkpatrick, Stephen Welch and Dominic Young have begun reviewing the bids tabled for the retailer, in the hopes of securing a sale before the crucial pre-Christmas trading period kicks off in earnest.
Gordon Brothers, Alvarez & Marsal and Poundland declined to comment.

items.body:
Wickes has officially opened its new store in Harrogate today (21st October), bringing its extensive range of home improvement products, expert advice and design services to local homeowners and trade professionals. The new store was officially opened by Harrogate Councillor Viv Poskit, marking the latest step in the retailer’s continued investment in its store network. The new store will be supported by a team of 21 colleagues, including 19 external hires, creating new employment opportunities in the local area.
Located on Ripon Road, Harrogate (HG1 2BS), the new store features 10,835 sq. ft. of ground floor space, alongside a 3,200 sq. ft. mezzanine housing a dedicated Kitchen and Bathroom showroom. Harrogate introduces a new small store format concept for Wickes, bringing together home improvement products, expert advice and inspiration under one roof. Digital screens throughout the store showcase Wickes’ products and services, helping customers explore ideas for projects of all sizes, from refreshing a room to planning a complete kitchen or bathroom transformation.
The Kitchen and Bathroom showroom allows customers to explore a range of designs and finishes, with Wickes’ Design Consultants on hand to provide the free Kitchen and Bathroom design service and help customers plan with confidence. Customers can also benefit from Wickes’ trusted installation service, alongside 15-minute Click & Collect and the Rapid Delivery service, which offers local orders delivered directly to customers’ doors within three hours, seven days a week, for an additional £6 delivery fee.
The new store features 100 rooftop solar panels, with a combined capacity of 30kW. Expected to generate approximately 41,880kWh of renewable electricity each year, the system supports Wickes’ ongoing investment in more sustainable stores by helping to reduce reliance on grid electricity and associated costs and carbon emissions.
Local trade people can stock up on project essentials, including timber, power tools and cement from trusted brands such as Bosch, Blue Circle and Knauf. TradePro members can save 10% on every purchase, alongside exclusive perks, fuel savings and ongoing rewards.
To celebrate the opening, customers can enjoy 15% off in store from Friday 30th October to Sunday 1st November. Wickes will also host a special decorating event in partnership with Dulux on Saturday 31st October. Customers will have the chance to meet the iconic Dulux dog, take a photo with the much-loved mascot and enter a competition to win Dulux merchandise, while picking up inspiration for their next decorating project.
Kate Thompson, head of property at Wickes, said: “We’re delighted to open our new store in Harrogate, bringing trusted home improvement products and expert advice to the local community. Our new small format store has been designed to make the most of the space, with a dedicated Kitchen and Bathroom showroom to help customers find inspiration and plan their projects with confidence. We’re also pleased to welcome 21 colleagues to the team and look forward to supporting local homeowners and trade professionals with their home improvement projects.”
The Wickes Community Programme has launched in Harrogate, supporting local charities and community groups with donated tools and materials to help improve community spaces. As part of the initiative, the new Harrogate store is supporting Mind Harrogate with supplies to create a partitioned corridor, allowing visitors to access the WC facilities without disrupting counselling sessions. This will help protect confidentiality and create a more private environment, enabling the charity to offer more one to one mental health sessions for the local community.

items.title: Carrefour maintains sales momentum, but unrest in France clouds its festive outlook, says GlobalData

Following today’s release of Carrefour’s figures for the three months ending 30 September 2026; Eleanor Simpson-Gould, senior retail analyst at GlobalData, a leading intelligence and productivity platform, offers her view: “Carrefour delivered another quarter of steady growth in Q3 2026. Group like-for-like (l-f-l) sales rose 2.3%, ahead of the 2.1% achieved in H1 with all […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
Following today’s release of Carrefour’s figures for the three months ending 30 September 2026; Eleanor Simpson-Gould, senior retail analyst at GlobalData, a leading intelligence and productivity platform, offers her view: “Carrefour delivered another quarter of steady growth in Q3 2026. Group like-for-like (l-f-l) sales rose 2.3%, ahead of the 2.1% achieved in H1 with all three core markets of France, Spain, and Brazil contributing positively. However, the escalating social and security situation in France has overshadowed this performance and forced the group to cut its full-year targets, just as it enters the most important trading period of the year. Carrefour now expects operating margin growth of between 0 and 15 basis points (bps), down from 25bps. It has also lowered its 2026 capital expenditure target to €1.6bn from €1.7bn by scaling back investment in France for the rest of the year, underlining how uncertain the final quarter has become. Carrefour’s strategic roadmap remains intact, and its commercial momentum in FY2026 is encouraging. However, the events in France expose the group’s dependence on its domestic market. Disruption from social unrest may persist in the run-up to the presidential election in May 2027, extending the pressure on profitability well beyond the festive period.
“France had been trading well, with l-f-l sales up 1.2% in Q3, a sixth consecutive quarter of growth, and the former Cora and Match stores continued gaining momentum. The disruption in the region has hit a significant number of urban stores, reducing footfall, shortening opening hours due to curfews, and raising security and logistics costs. With France accounting for more than half of group sales in Q3, the multinational has limited scope to offset weakness in other regions. Carrefour’s priority must be the safety of staff and customers, while its growing Drive and home delivery operations should be utilised to capture demand where stores face restrictions. Price investment must also become more targeted to protect margins in the short term. However, Carrefour must tread carefully, as many French households remain financial stretched with fuel prices close to record highs. Pulling back too far on price risks undoing the gains in price perception it has worked to build this year.
“Spain remains Carrefour’s most consistent market, with l-f-l sales up 2.1%, broadly in line with Q2, supported by sustained price leadership and a strong convenience performance. Carrefour should accelerate its convenience rollout, having opened 35 stores in Q3, as Spain’s resilience will be vital in cushioning group profitability while trading in France is disrupted.
“Brazil built on the stabilisation achieved in H1, with l-f-l sales rising 1.4% in Q3. Atacadão led the improvement, with growth of 2.0% up from 0.5% in Q2. This steady acceleration in a cash and carry market amid high interest rates suggests Atacadão is winning share, rather than benefiting from a market recovery. With nine-month l-f-l growth of just 0.4%, Brazil’s recovery is fragile and Carrefour needs to sustain Atacadão’s momentum and expand its Bulnez own-brand range to retain value-seeking shoppers while consumers remain under pressure.”

items.title: Back Market makes Slow Tech more affordable with three new launches, including The Outlet

At the second annual Slow Tech Summit in Paris today, Back Market announced the launch of The Back Market Outlet, a new lower-cost marketplace for smartphones and […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch!
